thread.title: Apple to offer free video content to device owners

author: Annlee Ellingson
title: Apple to offer free video content to device owners
text: – Staff Writer, L.A. Biz Oct 15, 2018, 6:09am HST Apple Inc. is spending a billion dollars on original content this year to get into the same business as Netflix, Amazon and Hulu, but so far it’s been unclear what the computer giant’s digital video service will look like. The industry got a glimpse this week thanks to a report from CNBC that said that Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) plans to put its shows on iPhones, iPads and Apple TVs in the pre-installed “TV” app. And owners of such devices will be able to watch Apple’s original content for free. Apple’s TV app will also house subscription channels from other companies, such as HBO, that users can pay for. The service is slated to debut in early 2019. Click here to read more. Meanwhile, here’s what else has been going on in the world of streaming this week: Pocket.watch repackages YouTube shows for Hulu, Amazon With tens of millions of subscribers across its YouTube channels, pocket.watch is repackaging its most popular videos into 22-minute episodes and putting them on Hulu and Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) with an eye toward selling them internationally as well. ( L.A. Biz ) Netflix app revenue soared 90% in Q2, pulling in an estimated $244 million Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX) has dramatically upped its revenue haul through smartphones. For the third quarter in a row, the streamer had the No. 1 grossing non-game mobile app worldwide in Q3 2018, generating around $243.7 million across both Apple’s App Store and Google Play, according to research firm Sensor Tower. ( Variety ) Katzenberg, Whitman reveal name of ‘NewTV’ — and the big-name talent who will make content for it For a couple of years now, Jeffrey Katzenberg has been working on a mysterious mobile-first media platform referred to as “NewTV.” Well, now it officially has a name: Quibi, for the “quick bites” of content it will deliver to consumers’ smartphones. ( L.A. Biz ) WarnerMedia to take on Netflix, Disney with its own streaming service Taking a page from The Walt Disney Co., WarnerMedia will launch its own Netflix-like direct-to-consumer streaming service in the fourth quarter of next year. The move follows the $85 billion acquisition of Time Warner Inc. by AT&T (NYS: T) this summer. ( L.A. Biz ) Disney appoints ESPN’s Aaron LaBerge as CTO of streaming and international division Aaron LaBerge , previously ESPN’s chief technology officer, is taking on a new role as executive vice president and CTO of Disney (NYSE: DIS)’s recently formed Direct-To-Consumer and International segment. LaBerge will be the first CTO of Direct-To-Consumer and International segment, reporting to chairman Kevin Mayer. ( Variety ) Netflix released record-high 676 hours of original programming in Q3 Netflix flooded its U.S. streaming service with an all-time high tonnage of original TV shows and movies in the third quarter of 2018 — a positive signal that the No. 1 subscription-video service will hit its customer-acquisition targets, according to a new report from Wall Street firm Cowen & Co. ( Variety ) Behind the deal for Netflix to invest $1 billion in New Mexico Five directors' chairs sat to the right of the big screen at Albuquerque Studios, reserved for a few who orchestrated one of New Mexico's biggest deal announcements in recent memory. “Welcome, Netflix,” said Keith Gardner, Gov. Susana Martinez's chief of staff. “That’s a woo-hoo, right?” ( Albuquerque Business First ) Walmart taps MGM to make content for Vudu Walmart Inc. (NYSE: WMT) is going Hollywood. The retail giant is partnering with MGM to create original programming for its Vudu digital video platform. Under the deal, MGM will make series based on IP from its film and television library. ( L.A. Biz )
